priceSeenAt: Sewing Machines Plus (sale price in search snippet; regular price $419.99)

stitchTypes.value: Basic, stretch and decorative stitches plus a built-in lettering font, marketed as 411 stitch applications; touch button stitch selection with LCD; 7 buttonhole styles

threadTrimmer.value: No thread cutter listed; a tie-off button is listed; the manual lists a hand thread knife for trimming ends (shared manual)

motor.value: Singer describes a powerful motor with extra high sewing speed; rated 0.7 A, 120 V, 60 Hz; wattage not published

frame.value: Full metal interior frame, stainless steel bedplate

dimensionsIn.value: 17.3 x 7.5 x 10.9 (W x D x H, Singer product page; Amazon lists 17.5 x 7.5 x 11)

includedFeet.value: 10 presser feet: all purpose, zipper, buttonhole, blind hem, button sewing, Sew Easy, satin stitch, even feed (walking), open toe and cording; 4 Class 15 transparent bobbins, large and small spool holders, spool pin felt, auxiliary spool pin, L screwdriver, brush and seam ripper, soft cover, pack of needles

warrantyUs.value: Limited 25/1 per Singer's product page and linked PDF: 25 years on the frame, 1 year on parts and adjustments; original purchaser, authorized sellers, household use

speedControl.value: Speed control lever sets the maximum sewing speed

claims: "Heavy Duty" (Singer series name; it is a model line, not a duty rating)
"a workhorse with endless possibilities" (Singer claim, repeated by dealers)
"powerful motor" with "extra high sewing speed" and "Professional speed for faster results" (Singer claims; no wattage published)
"designed with your heavy duty projects in mind, from denim to canvas" (Singer claim; no fabric thickness or layer rating published)
"a generous C space allows you to sew larger projects like quilts with ease" (Singer claim)

"Up to 25 Year Warranty Coverage" (Singer wording; the split is 25 years frame, 1 year parts)
conflicts: Speed: Singer's product page says 1100/min; the shared HD 6700C and HD 6705C manual says 1000 +/- 50 rpm. We use the manual figure; Amazon and dealers repeat 1,100.

Warranty: Singer's product page and linked PDF say 25/1 (25-year frame, 1-year parts); our earlier 25/2/90 is a tier Singer assigns to the 4452, 4432 and 3342, and Singer's coverage page does not name the 6700C. Amazon shows '1 Year Manufacturer'. The PDF names no model.

Needle up/down: the shared manual documents a Needle Up/Down button, the 6700C product page does not list it, and the 6800C and 6620C pages do. Our earlier 'none' came from a blog. Unresolved, so left [verify].

Stitch count: Singer's comparison page gives 200 built-in stitches and 411 applications; the product page gives 411 applications, and its prose also says 586, a figure that matches the 6800C page. Left [verify]; 586 is not used.
Lettering: Singer's product page lists 1 lettering font and its comparison page lists 2; the manual shows a Block Font at 7 mm letter height.
Throat: 6.4 in is Singer's 'needle to tower' figure, not stated as needle to body, so throat is [verify] on the rule 11 scale.
Weight: 7 kg (15.4 lb) in the shared manual against 14.6 lb on Amazon and 16.3 lb on one blog.
Start/stop: the shared manual documents a Start/Stop button; the product page does not list one. Unverified for the 6700C alone.
Sibling pages: Singer's comparison page gives the 6800C 8.3 in of throat and 1,050 spm while its 6800C product page says 6.4 in and 1100/min; read sibling rows with that in mind.
Page status on 2026-10-02 (page wording only): the Singer 6600C page returned 404 and the 6800C and 6620C pages read Out of Stock; the 6700C page showed the machine for sale.

ownerThemes.theme: Several owner help threads describe top thread looping mid-seam on a new 6700C after a clean test swatch; the answers point to rethreading through the tension discs, cleaning lint from the bobbin area, and the small bobbin case screw.
Walmart owner reviews (4 of 5 stars over about 200 reviews) call it smooth and good for quilting, curtains and clothing, with one experienced sewer saying it is not a first machine.
PatternReview members discussing the launch of Singer's computerized Heavy Duty line note that earlier HD models were all mechanical and question what the electronics add on a budget frame.

crossShop.why: Same head and frame with fewer stitches, no lettering and 5 feet, for about $30 less.
The mechanical Heavy Duty with a walking foot in the box; buyers weigh dials against an LCD.
The step up for quilters who want a wider harp and a knee lifter in a computerized machine.

editorial.verdict: A metal-frame computerized machine with 10 feet and a walking foot, but Singer's own pages disagree on speed, stitch count and needle up/down.
editorial.whoFor: A beginner or returning sewer who wants a walking foot, a speed lever and lettering on a metal-frame machine.
editorial.skipIf: You want a confirmed thread cutter or needle up/down button, a plain stitch count before you buy, or dials rather than an LCD on a heavy fabric machine.
editorial.keySpec: 1,000 rpm (manual) · 6.4 in needle to tower · 10 feet incl. walking foot · 15.4 lb
strengths: Singer's accessory list has 10 presser feet, including even feed (walking), open toe and cording feet, plus 4 Class 15 bobbins and a soft cover.
Singer lists a speed control lever that caps the sewing speed, adjustable presser foot pressure per the dealer listing, and 7 one-step buttonhole styles.
Singer describes a metal interior frame and stainless steel bed plate (a maker claim, not a duty rating).
weaknesses: Owners report threading and looping trouble (6 voices, 3 sources, including a needle threader that does not work for one Amazon reviewer).
Owners report tension problems (5 voices, 4 sources), such as a top tension dial that seems to have no effect.
Singer's product page lists no thread cutter; the 6800C page lists one.

checks.title: Needle up/down is unresolved
checks.body: The shared HD 6700C and HD 6705C manual documents a Needle Up/Down button. The 6700C product page does not list it, while the 6800C and 6620C pages do. Ask the seller to confirm for this exact model.

checks.title: Speed is 1000 or 1100
checks.body: Singer's product page says 1100/min; the shared manual says 1000 +/- 50 rpm. We show the manual figure and list both.

checks.title: Applications are not stitches
checks.body: Singer's comparison page says 200 built-in stitches and 411 applications. The product page prose also says 586, which looks like the 6800C figure. Check the stitch chart in the manual before comparing counts.

realCost: Extension table for quilting, sold separately or in a bundle; the base box does not include one.
Extra Class 15 transparent bobbins beyond the 4 included.
Hard case; only a soft cover is included.

faqs.q: How many stitches does the Singer 6700C have?
faqs.a: Singer's comparison page says 200 built-in stitches and 411 stitch applications. The product page says 411 applications and its prose also says 586, which looks like the 6800C number. We list the disagreement and do not state a plain count.

faqs.q: Does the 6700C have an automatic thread cutter?
faqs.a: Singer's product page lists a tie-off button and no thread cutter. The 6800C page lists a Thread Cutter Button that trims top and bottom threads. The manual's thread knife is a hand cutter.
Unresolved. The shared HD 6700C and HD 6705C manual documents a Needle Up/Down button, the 6700C product page does not list one, and the 6800C and 6620C pages do. Confirm with the seller.

faqs.q: Does the 6700C come with a walking foot?
faqs.a: Yes. The even feed (walking) foot is one of 10 feet on Singer's accessory list, along with open toe and cording feet.
6.4 in (163 mm), which Singer words as needle to tower. Singer does not state it as needle to body, so we treat it as [verify] on our throat scale.
Singer's product page says 1100/min. The shared manual says 1000 +/- 50 rpm at default length, and we use that figure.
7 kg, which is 15.4 lb, in the shared manual. Amazon lists 14.6 lb and one blog 16.3 lb.
Yes. Singer's product page lists 1 lettering font and its comparison page lists 2. The manual shows a Block Font at 7 mm letter height.
Singer claims a generous C space for larger projects like quilts. The throat is 6.4 in needle to tower, and one Walmart reviewer group calls it good for quilting. Treat larger quilts with caution.
Singer's product page and linked PDF say Limited 25/1: 25 years on the frame and 1 year on parts and adjustments. Singer's coverage page does not name the 6700C and Amazon shows 1 year.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the 6700C and the 6800C?
faqs.a: On Singer's pages the 6800C adds a thread cutter button, Needle Up/Down and more stitch applications (586 on its page). Singer's pages also disagree on the 6800C throat (6.4 in on its product page, 8.3 in on the comparison page) and speed (1100/min against 1,050).

faqs.q: How good is the evidence on owners?
faqs.a: Thin. We have 17 voices, 16 first-hand, from 16 Reddit threads (5 with the model in the title) and one retailer page; Amazon's 4.4 from 980 ratings is pooled across listings of this machine, and the Sewing Machines Plus page has 0 reviews. Reddit skews to help requests, so problems are over-represented.
